definitions.gloss: nothing at all; complete absence; nil
definitions.explanation: Emphatic way of saying there is absolutely nothing of something. Stronger than simply saying ない, it stresses the total lack or absence.

examples.japanese: {経験|けいけん}は{皆無|かいむ}だ。
この{地域|ちいき}では{犯罪|はんざい}が{皆無|かいむ}に{等|ひと}しい。
examples.english: Crime in this area is virtually nonexistent.

examples.japanese: {反対|はんたい}{意見|いけん}が{皆無|かいむ}だったので、{提案|ていあん}はそのまま{承認|しょうにん}された。
examples.english: Since there were no objections whatsoever, the proposal was approved as-is.

notes:
USAGE:
{皆無|かいむ} is a formal, emphatic expression. It is often used as a predicate ({皆無|かいむ}だ / {皆無|かいむ}である) or in the pattern {皆無|かいむ}に{等|ひと}しい ("virtually nonexistent").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {皆無|かいむ}に{等|ひと}しい (virtually nonexistent)
- {皆無|かいむ}である (to be completely absent)
- {経験|けいけん}{皆無|かいむ} (zero experience)

NUANCE:
More emphatic and literary than {全|まった}くない. Often appears in written or formal spoken contexts such as reports, speeches, and news articles.
